releases.name: aftermath 0.7.0
releases.body:
## aftermath 0.7.0

`init` now wires **only the agent you are running in**.

Previously `--host` defaulted to `all`, so an OpenCode session shelled out to
`claude plugin install` and `codex plugin marketplace add` (each cloning a
marketplace over the network) — and because `wireProject` never passed
`project: true`, those installs landed in the user's global `~/.claude` and
`~/.codex` instead of the project.

- `--host auto|opencode|claude|codex|all` — `auto` detects the running agent
  (`CLAUDECODE` → claude, `CODEX_*` → codex, else opencode); `AFTERMATH_HOST`
  overrides
- any Claude/Codex install triggered by `init` is project-scoped
  (`.claude/settings.json`), never global config
- empty arrays in `.aftermath/config.json` are regenerated, so a re-run picks
  up newly detected test commands / safe paths without `--force`
- `init` in an OpenCode session: **0.19s, zero agent-CLI calls**
- the Python port (`afm-recovery`) changed in lockstep; node↔python parity is
  enforced by tests

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/moah0911/aftermath/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

> This version was published to npm from a local checkout. The CI publish
> workflow skips when the version is already on npm, so it stays green.

releases.name: aftermath 0.5.1
releases.body: Post-failure recovery skill for AI coding agents: stop, revert cheap damage, return to last-known-good. Project-aware destructive guards, forward-edit freeze, checkpoints, and host parity for OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex.
